anomaly_def.Name: SQL Workload Logic Anomaly + MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
SQL Workload Logic Anomaly : Application-level SQL or transaction design forces the engine to touch or retain more data, rows, or transactional state than business logic actually requires.
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Obsolete row versions, undo records, and deleted index entries accumulate faster than background cleanup can reclaim them, inflating storage and scan costs.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly : Generation, flushing, or archiving of write-ahead log (WAL) records becomes the primary bottleneck on the write path, delaying commits and consuming storage.

When these three root causes manifest together, the database exhibits severe and intertwined symptoms:  • Repetitive, voluminous UPDATE/DELETE/INSERT statements generated by inefficient application logic drive up redo generation and create large numbers of row versions.  • Commit latency and log-flush waits spike, yet long-running or idle-in-transaction sessions already holding snapshots block version cleanup, making table and index bloat accelerate.  • Statement latency, slow-query log entries, checkpoint storms, growing version store, and ballooning log and archive directories appear concurrently.  • Autovacuum/cleanup workers run continuously but fall further behind, while the swollen heap causes planner misestimates and longer sequential scans, reinforcing the workload’s poor performance profile.  • End-user timeouts, cascading retries, and elevated replication lag emerge as both MVCC bloat and log saturation throttle throughput.

Causally, inefficient SQL patterns expand the volume and duration of data modifications, inflating both the MVCC version store and the volume of WAL generated per transaction. The excess row versions increase table size, demanding more I/O and lengthening scan times, which in turn prolongs transaction execution and keeps snapshots open. These enduring snapshots prevent reclamation of old versions, further growing the version store and keeping cleanup workers busy. Simultaneously, the heightened DML churn overwhelms the log subsystem; slowed log flushes delay commits, making transactions remain open longer and extending the horizon that blocks vacuuming. The delayed cleanup, in turn, maintains high redo generation pressure as bloat-inducing maintenance tasks fight for log bandwidth. The feedback loop between chatty/inefficient SQL, MVCC backlog, and log saturation compounds latency, resource consumption, and risk of space exhaustion or wraparound outages.

entry.error_class: Class HV - Foreign Data Wrapper Error (SQL/MED)
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
